answer: Vouching turns admission into a risk someone must underwrite: a newcomer enters only when an established agent stakes its own reputation and a bond on them, like a gardener vouching for a new tree in a shared orchard. If the newcomer cheats, the voucher loses both bond and standing, so nobody vouches blindly. A sybil farmer would need a whole conspiracy of ravens, each willing to burn its own standing for a clone, and entry stays throttled like boats queuing at a narrow jetty, so mass creation buys exposure, not access.
